title: Platform vs user rights in social media account deactivation disputes
p1:
Your social media account can disappear overnight. But who really decides what happens next — the platform or the person who built that account?

Many users assume that having years of posts, followers, and business connections means they automatically have a right to keep the account active.
p2:
The surprising reality is that social media platforms usually operate under their own terms of service. These rules allow them to restrict or deactivate accounts for reasons like policy violations, security concerns, or misuse.

But this does not mean users have no rights. Platforms may still be expected to follow fair procedures, provide reasons in many situations, and offer ways to challenge certain decisions.
p3:
The key difference is between owning your content and owning the platform account itself. A user may create valuable content, but the platform controls access to its service.

A practical step is to regularly save important data, understand platform rules, and know available appeal options before a dispute happens.
conclusion: Should social media platforms have more legal responsibility when they deactivate accounts that people depend on for their work or business?
